It's a very thin cream and I got it because of that apple butter description, but it has a funny, almost funky oil smell. I've used it a few times but I'm struggling to continue to use it because it just leaves my skin with this weird residue feeling that somehow both oily and slightly dry at the same time. It seems like it might help with moisture a little bit but I've had to use a lot of it to get any notable effect. I would not buy this again and you probably shouldn't either. When I first started using this cleansing balm, I'm not going to lie, I thought that it may be just a little too rich for my oily-leaning combination type skin. However, I have now come to very much appreciate it for its gentle, soothing nature. When I first rinsed it off I felt like it left a very fine moisturizing layer on my skin, but after my skin had dried I was simply left with a cleansed yet hydrated feeling. I almost feel like, with my skin type, this cleanser is so nourishing that I could skip the moisturizer; at least with the humid, summertime weather that I'm currently experiencing. I also wasn't sure if this cleansing balm would play well with my acne-prone skin, but I'm happy to say that they get along quite nicely. In fact, I have been using an acne-treatment that is a bit drying and actually causes my skin some peeling, but this cleanser has been really helpful at mitigating its drying effects. To conclude my thoughts, I think that this cleansing balm is perfectly suitable to almost any skin type, however, I do feel that it would work especially well for those who have drier skin types. I also think that this is a product that can work for any time of year, but would be particularly wonderful for the drier autumn & winter months when, more often than not, our skin could use a little extra nourishment. So, with all that being said, I do enjoy this cleansing balm very much and would happily recommend it to anyone looking for a deeply nourishing, moisturizing cle
